text:
Vikram: Heads-up — ran an AWQ quantization path for llama-13b-v2 this morning; saw a small but consistent NLI accuracy regression when prefix cache and continuous batching are both enabled. Wanted to call it out before the full bakeoff.

Maria: Can you drop the numbers?

Vikram: Quick snapshot from the nightly run: 
- FP16 baseline (no quant): NLI acc = 92.1%
- AWQ quant + prefix cache + continuous_batch_ms=20: NLI acc = 90.2%
- AWQ quant + cache disabled: NLI acc = 91.9%
- GPTQ int8 path: NLI acc = 91.8%

So looks like the quality delta only shows up for AWQ when cache+cont-batching are on. Latency with cache on is ~12% better though.

Ken: Curious about runtime config and cache key dtype. Could be a dtype/format mismatch between packed AWQ keys and our cache layer.

Vikram: Service config (sanitized):
```
model: llama-13b-v2-awq
quantization: awq
prefix_cache:
  enabled: true
continuous_batching:
  enabled: true
  window_ms: 20
```
Eval command used:
```
./eval_harness --model endpoint://redwood/llama-13b-v2-awq --task nli --split dev --batch 64
```

Ken: Hunch: AWQ stores packed int8/blocks for KV. Our prefix cache expects float32 keys (we dequantize on read), so if a write stores packed bytes and a subsequent read expects floats we might sometimes match incorrectly. Any log evidence?

Vikram: Pulled debug logs: 
```
[debug] kv_lookup: model=llama-13b-v2-awq shard=3 key_shape=(16,256)
[warn] kv_cache: stored_dtype=float32 expected_dtype=int8_lookup
[debug] dequantize_latency_ms=0.8
```

Adele: Sounds like a dtype mismatch. Repro plan:
1) Disable continuous batching (set window_ms=0) to see if merging requests amplifies the issue.
2) Try AWQ with cache enabled but force dequantize-on-store (so cache always holds float32 keys).
3) Compare perf vs quality: measure NLI and latency p95/token cost.

We should run a 3-arm staging AB test:
- route 80% -> FP16 baseline
- route 10% -> AWQ + cache + cont_batching
- route 10% -> AWQ + cache + cont_batching_disabled

Vikram: I tried forcing dequantize-on-store locally: NLI recovered to 91.8% (nearly baseline). Latency penalty was ~6% vs fully packed AWQ+cache.

Maria: If dequantize-on-store fixes quality, we can add a model-level flag: awq_prefers_dequantize_cache = true and gate it behind opt-in initially.

Ken: Longer term: runtime should support quantization-aware comparisons for cache lookups instead of relying on float buffers. I'll draft an RFC for a small kv-compare-hook that understands packed formats. Should be low-risk but needs perf testing.

Vikram: Does continuous batching make this worse because multiple inflight requests end up reading/writing mixed-format cache entries without a barrier?

Ken: Exactly. Continuous batching groups requests across tight windows; if thread A writes packed bytes and thread B reads expecting floats, you can get partial/incorrect prefix matches. Options: always dequantize-on-write, add a cache-schema/version tag per entry, or implement the kv-compare-hook that is format-aware.

Adele: For the bakeoff I'll run these arms:
- FP16 baseline
- AWQ + cache (dequantize-on-store)
- AWQ + cache (packed store)
- AWQ + cache + continuous_batching=20
I'll collect NLI, PIQA, a small hallucination probe, token/p95 latency, and throughput metrics.

Vikram: Infra scheduled a staging rollout window for the AB test at 2025-03-14T09:00Z.

infra-bot: Deploy plan created: rollout/staging/awq-cache-bake-20250314 — CI checks pending :gear:

Maria: I'll own the eval harness runs and will post CSVs here. I'll also add a small toggle script for dequantize-on-store so others can reproduce exactly.

Ken: Opened a draft PR for kv-compare-hook: https://git.redwood/infra/kv-compare-proto — PTAL.

Vikram: If dequantize-on-store is acceptable perf-wise we can ship it as a model policy. If not, Ken's hook is the fallback.

Adele: Running the jobs now, will share artifacts and a short summary in ~45m. :hourglass_flowing_sand: 

Maria: :eyes:

Ken: :thumbsup:
